content:
> Can find nowhere on Thunderbird that shows different in and out settings.

Incoming is here: Account Settings > Server Settings for the account

I can see you are using an IMAP Mail Server For BT you would use: Incoming

  • Server name: mail.btinternet.com
  • Port : 993
  • User name = full bt email address
  • Connection Security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication Method: Normal Password

Outgoing SMTP is here:

  • In Account Settings
  • Left Pane - scroll to bottom and look below 'Local Folders'
  • You will see 'Outgoing Server (SMTP)' - click on it
  • On the right you will now see a list of all your outgoing smtp servers.
  • Select the one which has username= email address of account
  • Click on 'Edit'

BT SMTP server settings: Outgoing SMTP

  • Description: Type BT email address, so not to confuse with any other account
  • Server name: mail.btinternet.com
  • Port : 465
  • Connection Security: SSL/TLS
  • Authentication Method: Normal Password
  • User name = full bt email address

click on 'OK

In 'Account Settings'

  • select name of account in left pane
  • Look bottom right for 'Outgoing Server (SMTP)' this should be pointing specifically to the BT outgoing server for the account. This is you see how useful it was to enter the SMTP 'Description' as BT email address, because if it does not show what you typed then you may be using the wrong SMTP.
  • So if wrong - click on the drop down and select correct smtp.
  • DO NOT click on the 'Edit SMTP_Server' button because that is only used if you are absolutely certain you are using correct smtp server and it's very rare you should need to edit a correct server.

You might want to keep a copy of this info just in case you ever need it.

There are 3 different types of Search. It's always helpful if you explicitly state the method used.

Global Search (Ctrl+K) which searches on everything.

Quick Filter (Ctrl+Shift+K) searches on a preselected folder

Via Menu app icon Tools > 'Search Messages' (Ctrl+Shift+F) OR Via Menu Bar Toolbar Edit > Find > 'Search Messages' (Ctrl+Shift+F) This search can search on specific folders or accounts and search on a specific range of parameters.

No results can mean there are no results specifically using the parameters you inputted.

It really depends upon method chosen and parameters set. It also depends upon whether you have downloaded full copies because searching on the body of emails that have not been downloaded is not going to be useful.

I'm not sure how Thunderbird can understand your expectations of results. More info would be helpful.

What OS are you using ? What version of Thunderbird are you using ? Where did you get the installation of Thunderbird eg: Official thunderbird download webpage, Windows App Store, Snap, Flatpak etc ? Perhaps you could upload image(s) showing example and stating which search is being used and what parameters/conditions are being set.
